title: Local network evolution rules driving shortest path multiplicity
summary: The shortest path multiplicity, here denoted by $μ$, is an important metric of complex networks. For real networks $μ$ is high and it correlates with the network community structure. Since local network evolution induces network communities, it is possible that a high shortest path multiplicity is the natural expectation of local evolution rules. Here I demonstrate, by means of numerical simulations and exact results, that this is indeed the case.
